description:
Proposal: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-gl6.18.html (approved 2026-11-11), step 1. No behaviour change.

Today each scheduler (JIT Runtime in src/exec/runtime.rs, interpreter adapter in src/ir_interp/backend.rs, AotScheduler in runtime/src/aot_shim.rs) keeps its own copy of reporting: after end_quantum it emits QuantumEnd::collection (emit_gc) and on Disposition::Exited calls ExitRecord::emit; send paths call emit_send_probe; about_to_sleep raises SCHEDULER_SLEPT; teardown calls emit_run_ended. AOT drops all of them (aot_shim.rs:453, :586). The interpreter alone raises fz.runtime.send_to_unknown_pid.

Change:
- New runtime/src/telemetry.rs: RuntimeEvent<'a> { ExecutionReady, ProcessExited(&Process), SchedulerSlept(Duration), SendProbe(&SendProbe), Gc(&Collection), RunEnded(RunEnded) }; the event names (moved from exec/runtime.rs); RunEnded moved from the host with a sample(before) constructor; write_line(out, time_ns, span_id, parent_span_id, &RuntimeEvent) producing exactly today's JSONL line (process_exited keeps its nested "process":{"opaque_type":"fz_runtime::process::Process",...} shape).
- Scheduler::observe(&mut self, RuntimeEvent), required (no default), replaces about_to_sleep. end_quantum observes Gc right after collecting and ProcessExited after the exit drain_destructors (so dtors_dispatched still counts exit destructors). QuantumEnd collapses to the Disposition (delete the struct if it carries only that).
- Host: one emit_runtime_event(tel, RuntimeEvent) raising the same typed raw events as today; it replaces emit_gc, emit_send_probe, emit_run_ended, ExitRecord::emit and the direct SCHEDULER_SLEPT raises. JIT Runtime and the interp adapter implement observe with it; send paths and teardown call it. ProcessExitCapture and other typed captures keep working.
- JsonlBackend's handlers for the six runtime events append write_line output (still under the public-trace allowlist); delete the five host projections incl. the Process opaque branch in jsonl.rs (~1741) if nothing else uses it.
- AotScheduler implements observe as an explicit no-op; its send hook passes the probe it used to drop.

Removals in this commit: QuantumEnd::collection; three post-end_quantum emit blocks; Scheduler::about_to_sleep; emit_gc/emit_send_probe/emit_run_ended/ExitRecord::emit; host-owned GC/SEND_PROBE/RUN_ENDED/SCHEDULER_SLEPT constants; host runtime projections; fz.runtime.send_to_unknown_pid (interp-only; its JSONL handler and the drive_test.rs:9251 absence assertion go with it); GcStats::list_tail_edges, resource_heap_edges, resource_scalar_slots and their increments in heap/gc/trace.rs (written, never read).

Prediction: run and interp JSONL runtime lines for fixtures 00901, 00910, 00911, 00687 byte-identical to d1913f2ec after removing time_ns; no test pin moves.

Done when: the above, the prediction checked and reported; .agent/docs/runtime-telemetry.md states one observe and one writer and no longer claims AOT behaves identically; scheduler-zero-arg-closures.md updated; grep for removed names over .agent, guides, README.md, fixtures returns nothing; full gate green (cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace --all-targets --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=1; cargo test --workspace --doc); commit in Why / What changed / Verification form; no co-author trailer, no attribution line.
title: The scheduling core reports each runtime event through one required observe, and one writer renders its line
